name: r7_from_c1e7

name: r7_from_e2e4
comment: The `lcall 0xE2E4` at 0xDA78 is followed by `mov A,R7` at 0xDA7B and a test on it, so this is the callee's return value; the decompiler models it as a flag it also assigns zero to. The callee is `poll_d78a_for_indices_0_and_1` (ec/decompiled/pd/E2E4.asm): it runs R2 from 0 up to 1, loading R7 to the index and calling 0xD78A on each pass. Its `mov R7, #0x1` at 0xE320 sits immediately before the `ret` at 0xE322 and overwrites R7 on every path, and 0xE2E4 has no other exit, so it returns R7 = 1 whatever 0xD78A left on the second pass. The R7 tested here is therefore that constant, not 0xD78A's result passed through, and the `jz 0xDA4D` at 0xDA7C is not taken on this path: the arm after it is reached every time this call site is. 0xD78A (ec/decompiled/pd/D78A.asm) does set R7 = 1 or 0 on each of its own exits, so 0xE2E4 consumes those two results -- it just does not return them, and nothing here shows a test of either. Whether the branch was meant to test 0xD78A's second result is not established by these instructions.
